literature.headline_zh: 狂犬病病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期重点文献按发表日期、相关性、证据等级和研究质量综合排序，研究结果与综述证据分别核验后形成以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在检查的 51 例疑似病例中,46 例(90.2%)经实验室确诊为狂犬病。家养狗占提交内容的 96.1%,而猫则占 3.9%。大多数可疑动物要么未接种疫苗(64.7%),要么疫苗接种状况未知(33.3%),据报道,90.2%的动物在提交前曾咬伤过人类。 [paper-963b1a18a14523fa]
确定了六个主要主题: 狂犬病死亡焦虑。医疗焦虑和寻求安慰。家庭保护和社会影响。污染恐惧和避免。以及对自由漫步的狗的有争议的态度。死亡焦虑(26%)和寻求医疗保证(30%)是最常见的主题类别。 [paper-78c12539ae601d62]
尸检显示脑组织中存在病毒抗原(通过直接荧光抗体 31 测试)和病毒 RNA(通过实时 RTPCR)。 [paper-784af4221daac0f4]
八项实地随机对照试验 (RCT) 表明,与对照相比,One Health 干预措施有效减少了疾病发生或病原体检测。典型的做法包括全面的多领域干预措施、参与性方法、长期结果评估、方法三角测量、对结果的谨慎解释以及描述干预措施的视觉辅助工具。 [paper-6cc8d7c282a20794]
延误医疗护理与发烧(65.6%)为主要症状有关。 [paper-d4460c2146ff116f]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.caveats_zh: 部分证据来自摘要、观察性研究或叙述性综述，结论应结合研究设计和证据等级理解。
literature.brief_en: The literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.

news.headline_zh: 狂犬病病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期新闻简报仅纳入获得有效正文或实质性来源摘要、并通过病原相关性和翻译门禁的报道。
key_findings_zh: 向乌克兰运送 2,000 瓶狂犬病免疫球蛋白,以便紧急分发给抗狂犬病护理中心。乌克兰新闻社和卫生部报道。 [news-9d292b25aee3bf10]
布莱恩县的一只蝙蝠狂犬病检测呈阳性。中南部公共卫生区报告了这一发现并向公众通报。状态已确认。 [news-be003f3d75acf511]
WOAH 报告称,检测到海狗体内存在持续狂犬病传播。 [news-ac20fab40cf3662c]
科罗拉多州的一名兽医组织了一场虚拟 5K 活动,为华盛顿州立大学 (WSU) 在坦桑尼亚的狂犬病控制项目筹集资金。据报道,该活动是受坦桑尼亚之旅启发而发起的一项首创活动,并计划使其成为一年一度的传统活动。这是报告的筹款活动,而不是疫情或已确认的公共卫生事件。 [news-214d02c6305a253a]
蒙大拿州畜牧部官员就今年夏天野生动物中狂犬病病例的增加发出公开警告,强调全州范围内的蝙蝠和蒙大拿州东南部的臭鼬。该警告是基于已确认的患有狂犬病的动物和报告的暴露情况。 [news-30d276da1315fa3a]

papers.title: Analysis of health anxiety trajectories in rabies exposure patients based on machine learning
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To identify the dynamic evolution trajectory of health anxiety in patients with initial rabies exposure and to conduct predictive analysis of health anxiety trajectories using machine learning algorithms. METHODS: A total of 548 rabies exposure patients from a tertiary hospital in Nanning were selected between January 2024 and October 2025. Health anxiety levels were assessed at 0, 3, 7, 14, and 28 days post-exposure using the Health Anxiety Scale following a 5-dose immunization schedule. A latent variable growth mixture model was employed to identify anxiety development trajectories. Six machine learning algorithms were utilized to establish a high-risk health anxiety identification model, and a comprehensive evaluation of the model's performance was conducted, with the SHAP algorithm used for model interpretation. RESULTS: All 548 patients completed the survey. The latent variable growth mixture model identified three health anxiety development trajectories: low-level anxiety-stable group, moderate to high-level anxiety-improving group, and high persistent anxiety-hard to relieve group. Multivariate logistic regression analysis indicated that being female, having a college degree or higher, high rabies knowledge, a greater number of comorbidities, level III exposure, and delayed medical treatment were independent risk factors belonging to the 'high persistent anxiety-hard to relieve group.' In contrast, a higher level of health literacy was identified as a protective factor. The XGBoost model demonstrated superior predictive performance on the independent test set, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.881, while SHAP analysis ensured clinical interpretability. SHAP analysis of the XGBoost model revealed that health literacy, Perceived social support, rabies knowledge, Payment method and Animal source were the five most important features predicting the 'high persistent group. CONCLUSION: There is heterogeneity in the health anxiety trajectories of patients exposed to rabies. A predictive model based on machine learning can facilitate the early identification of high-risk individuals, providing a basis for implementing precise psychological interventions.

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:识别狂犬病初次暴露患者健康焦虑的动态演变轨迹,并利用机器学习算法对健康焦虑轨迹进行预测分析。方法:选取2024年1月至2025年10月期间南宁市某三级医院狂犬病暴露患者548例,按5剂次免疫方案,采用健康焦虑量表评估暴露后0、3、7、14、28天的健康焦虑水平。采用潜在变量增长混合模型来识别焦虑发展轨迹。利用6种机器学习算法建立高危健康焦虑识别模型,并对模型性能进行综合评价,并采用SHAP算法进行模型解释。结果:548 名患者全部完成了调查。潜变量增长混合模型确定了三种健康焦虑发展轨迹:低水平焦虑稳定组、中高水平焦虑改善组和高持续焦虑难以缓解组。多因素logistic回归分析显示,女性、大学本科及以上学历、狂犬病知识较高、合并症较多、III级暴露、延迟就医是“高持续性焦虑难以缓解组”的独立危险因素。相比之下,较高水平的健康素养被认为是一个保护因素。XGBoost 模型在独立测试集上表现出卓越的预测性能,受试者工作特征曲线下面积为 0.881,而 SHAP 分析确保了临床可解释性。XGBoost 模型的 SHAP 分析显示,健康素养、感知社会支持、狂犬病知识、支付方式和动物来源是预测“高持续性群体”的五个最重要特征。结论:狂犬病暴露患者的健康焦虑轨迹存在异质性。基于机器学习的预测模型有助于早期识别高危人群,为实施精准心理干预提供基础。

papers.title: Fear of rabies and post-bite psychological stress: a qualitative study of YouTube comments from India
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Dog-mediated rabies remains a fatal yet preventable zoonotic disease and continues to cause a substantial proportion of global rabies deaths in India. Although biomedical and epidemiological aspects are well documented, far less attention has been paid to the psychological impact of rabies exposure and the public fear surrounding it. Objective To explore how rabies is perceived and emotionally experienced in public online discourse in India, and to characterise patterns of anxiety and distress expressed following dog-bite exposure. Methods Public comments (n = 300) were retrieved from six Indian YouTube videos featuring rabies-related content, including news debates, medical explanations, fatal case narratives, free-roaming-dog attack footage, and short videos referencing post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP). Following screening for relevance, 172 comments were analysed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase inductive thematic analysis framework. Results Six principal themes were identified: Rabies Death Anxiety; Medical Anxiety and Reassurance Seeking; Family Protection and Social Impact; Contamination Fear and Avoidance; Hypervigilance; and Contested Attitudes towards Free-Roaming Dogs. Fear-oriented themes predominated. Death anxiety (26%) and medical reassurance seeking (30%) were the most frequent thematic categories. Many comments described persistent rumination, repeated wound-checking, uncertainty regarding vaccine adequacy, and ongoing distress long after exposure. Family-level behavioural changes and avoidance practices were also described. Comments also revealed contrasting views on free-roaming dogs, ranging from support for humane vaccination, sterilisation and coexistence to calls for removal or culling. Conclusion The analysed social media discourse suggests that rabies is represented not only as a biomedical threat, but also as a source of persistent uncertainty and fear. Digital comment spaces reveal uncertainty, fear of fatality, and behavioural adaptation following perceived exposure. Integrating psychological considerations and clear risk communication into rabies-control programmes may strengthen public confidence in prevention and treatment strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dog-mediated rabies remains a fatal yet preventable zoonotic disease and causes a substantial proportion of global rabies deaths in India, yet psychological impacts of exposure and public fear are understudied. The study aimed to explore how rabies is perceived and emotionally experienced in public online discourse in India, and to characterise patterns of anxiety and distress expressed following dog-bite exposure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A qualitative thematic analysis was conducted on public comments retrieved from six Indian YouTube videos featuring rabies-related content. A total of 172 comments were analysed after screening for relevance.
analysis.methods: Public comments (n = 300) were retrieved from six Indian YouTube videos, including news debates, medical explanations, fatal case narratives, free-roaming-dog attack footage, and short videos referencing post-exposure prophylaxis. Thematic analysis was performed using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase inductive framework.
analysis.main_results: Six principal themes were identified: Rabies Death Anxiety. Medical Anxiety and Reassurance Seeking. Family Protection and Social Impact. Contamination Fear and Avoidance. and Contested Attitudes towards Free-Roaming Dogs. Death anxiety (26%) and medical reassurance seeking (30%) were the most frequent thematic categories.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study interprets rabies as a source of persistent uncertainty and fear beyond its biomedical threat, highlighting how digital comment spaces reveal ongoing distress and behavioural adaptations following perceived exposure. This qualitative exploration of public discourse on rabies in India is novel in focusing on psychological impacts rather than clinical or epidemiological aspects.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Integrating psychological considerations and clear risk communication into rabies-control programmes may strengthen public confidence in prevention and treatment strategies. Findings suggest that addressing fear and uncertainty could improve adherence to post-exposure prophylaxis and reduce unnecessary distress.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on YouTube comments, which may not represent the broader population and are subject to selection and reporting biases. The evidence strength is moderate due to the qualitative nature of the analysis and the absence of quantitative validation or triangulation with other data sources.

analysis.summary_en: This qualitative study analysed 172 YouTube comments from six Indian rabies-related videos to explore public perceptions and emotional responses to rabies exposure. Six themes emerged, with death anxiety (26%) and medical reassurance seeking (30%) being most frequent. The findings reveal persistent uncertainty, fear of fatality, and behavioural adaptations such as rumination and avoidance practices. The study interprets rabies as a dual threat—biomedical and psychological—highlighting the need for psychological support and clear risk communication in rabies-control programmes. While novel in its focus on public discourse, the evidence is limited by selection bias and qualitative scope, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 狗介导的狂犬病仍然是一种致命但可预防的人畜共患疾病,在印度导致全球狂犬病死亡的很大一部分,但暴露和公众恐惧的心理影响尚未得到充分研究。该研究旨在探讨印度公众在线讨论中如何看待狂犬病和在情感上体验狂犬病,并描述被狗咬伤后表达的焦虑和痛苦模式。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对从六个包含狂犬病相关内容的印度 YouTube 视频中检索到的公众评论进行了定性主题分析。经过相关性筛选后,总共对 172 条评论进行了分析。
analysis_zh.methods: 公众评论 (n = 300) 是从 6 个印度 YouTube 视频中检索的,包括新闻辩论、医学解释、致命病例叙述、自由漫步的狗攻击镜头以及涉及暴露后预防的短视频。使用布劳恩和克拉克的六阶段归纳框架进行主题分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 确定了六个主要主题: 狂犬病死亡焦虑。医疗焦虑和寻求安慰。家庭保护和社会影响。污染恐惧和避免。以及对自由漫步的狗的有争议的态度。死亡焦虑(26%)和寻求医疗保证(30%)是最常见的主题类别。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究将狂犬病解释为超出其生物医学威胁的持续不确定性和恐惧的根源,强调数字评论空间如何揭示感知暴露后持续的痛苦和行为适应。这种对印度狂犬病公众讨论的定性探索是新颖的,它关注的是心理影响而不是临床或流行病学方面。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 将心理考虑和明确的风险沟通纳入狂犬病控制计划可能会增强公众对预防和治疗策略的信心。研究结果表明,解决恐惧和不确定性可以提高对暴露后预防的依从性并减少不必要的痛苦。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖 YouTube 评论而受到限制,这些评论可能无法代表更广泛的人群,并且会受到选择和报告偏差的影响。由于分析的定性性质以及缺乏与其他数据源的定量验证或三角测量,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Characterization of an Arctic-like 1a rabies virus from a 54-day-old puppy with atypical presentation, Pune, India, 2026
papers.abstract: Abstract Rabies remains a significantly underreported fatal zoonosis in India, where the Arctic-like 1a (AL1a) lineage predominates in dog populations. While atypical clinical presentations in dogs can delay diagnosis and increase human exposure risk, genomic and clinical data on neonatal canine rabies remain limited. This study reports an exceptional case of rabies in a 54-day old unvaccinated German shepherd puppy which presented with severe pruritus and self-biting behaviour. The puppy was euthanized due to poor clinical response. Post-mortem testing revealed viral antigen (by Direct Fluorescent Antibody Test) and viral RNA (by real-time RTPCR) in the brain tissue. Whole-genome sequencing recovered a near-complete rabies virus genome (11,947 nucleotides; 99.5% genome coverage), classified within the AL1a_A1.1 sublineage. Phylogenetic analysis revealed close genetic relatedness to contemporary Indian rabies virus strains. Comparative genomic analysis identified 4, 3, 6, and 8 non-synonymous substitutions in the phosphoprotein, matrix, glycoprotein, and polymerase genes, respectively. This case is one of the youngest documented cases of canine rabies with atypical manifestations, caused by the AL1a viral clade. Our findings highlight the risks associated with neonatal canine rabies, the need for heightened clinical suspicion in atypical cases, and the importance of genomic surveillance to monitor evolving rabies virus lineages in endemic regions.

Phylogenetic analysis revealed close genetic relatedness to contemporary Indian rabies virus strains. Comparative genomic analysis identified 4, 3, 6, and 8 non-synonymous substitutions in the phosphoprotein, matrix, glycoprotein, and polymerase genes, respectively. This case is one of the youngest documented cases of canine rabies with atypical manifestations, caused by the AL1a viral clade. Our findings highlight the risks associated with neonatal canine rabies, the need for heightened clinical suspicion in atypical cases, and the importance of genomic surveillance to monitor evolving rabies virus lineages in endemic regions.

Rabies claims around 59,000 human lives and thousands of livestock 45 globally every year (1), though death estimates from global rabies burden studies range from 20,000 to 46 175,000 (2). Dog-mediated human rabies deaths persist in more than 100 countries (2). While high- 47 income countries have nearly eliminated canine rabies, the disease remains endemic in developing 48 countries in Asia and Africa (3). India remains a global rabies hotspot, reporting about 36% of the global 3 49 human rabies deaths (1). The authors have recently identified an atypical canine case 69 of rabies in an adult dog which presented with aggravation of epilepsy. RABV replication within dorsal 70 root ganglia can result in localized or generalized intense pruritus and is frequently seen in patients with 71 rabies (8). 72 Despite the well-documented epidemiology of Arctic-like 1a strains in India, comprehensive genomic 73 characterization attempts of such strains associated with neonatal canine rabies have been rare. The puppy was dewormed with oral fenbendazole (one dose each on 81 24th, 25th and 26th April), and vaccinated against canine parvovirus and distemper (Puppy DP) on 27th 82 March 2026. On 4th April, the puppy presented with complaints of severe itching of the lower back and 83 inguinal area, and was treated with intramuscular ceftriaxone and prednisolone followed by oral 84 amoxicillin-clavulanic acid (0.9 mL bd) and gabapentin (25 mg, hs) starting the next day. On 5th April, 85 the puppy again presented with intense itching and self-biting. On examination, there was constant 86 itching on the right ear, belly and side of the trunk. The pupillary light reflex was normal, and there was 87 no nystagmus. Fleas were noted around the head. The puppy was treated with oral cetirizine (4 mL od) 88 and enrofloxacin-silver sulphadiazine ear drops (o.d. and s.o.s.). On 7th April, the puppy had one episode 89 of vomiting, persistent itching of the right ear, biting of the right thigh, and was vocalizing constantly. 90 Hematological tests revealed leucocytosis (29,000 cells/mm3), lymphopenia (4.5%), neutrophilia 91 (90.9%), and thrombocytosis (574,000 cells/mm3). An X-ray of the skull was unremarkable. 92 Biochemical testing revealed serum creatinine of 0.24 mg/dL, serum glutamic pyruvic transaminase 93 of 41 U/L, serum sodium of 144 mEq/L, serum potassium of 4.3 mEq/L, and serum chloride of 113 94 mEq/L. The puppy was treated with oral ranitidine (0.3 mL t.d.s.), augmentin (1.1 mL b.d.), Relaxzyme- 95 S (1 o.d.), gabapentin (15 mg, o.d.), ondansetron (3.1 mL b.d.) and Comfoderm spray (anti- 96 inflammatory). By 8th April, the puppy had 3 episodes of vomiting. On examination, the puppy was 97 hyperactive, biting aimlessly, vocalizing constantly, and febrile (initially 103°F, then 105°F). Rapid 98 lateral flow antigen tests for canine parvovirus and rabies performed at the clinic yielded negative 99 results. On 9th April, the puppy was active but mostly recumbent, had two episodes of vomiting, and 100 exhibited microseizures and chorea. The puppy was started on intravenous fluids, and treated with 101 intravenous pantoprazole (40 mg), ceftriaxone (1000 mg), ondansetron (30 mL), oral phenobarbital (0.6 5 102 mL bd) and oral gabapentine (50 mg, 1 od). Lateral flow rapid antigen test for canine distemper virus 103 yielded a negative result. During the period of sickness, three family members suffered bites from the 104 puppy and sought post-exposure rabies prophylaxis. In view of poor clinical outcome, the puppy was 105 euthanized on 9th April, 2026. 106 Methods 107 Post-mortem brain tissue of the puppy was transported to the Rabies Laboratory under cold chain 108 conditions and processed immediately. 109 Direct Fluorescent Antibody Test for rabies 110 Impression smears were prepared from the tissue, and a Direct Fluorescent Antibody Test was 111 performed using a FITC anti-rabies monoclonal globulin (Fujirebio, Inc.) as per manufacturer 112 instructions. 113 Real-time PCR for rabies 114 Total RNA was extracted from 100 mg of the tissue specimen using TRIzolTM reagent (Thermo 115 Scientific) as per manufacturer instructions. TaqMan real-time reverse transcription polymerase chain 116 reaction (RTPCR) for rabies virus was performed using a standard protocol (9). The assay was 117 performed using 5 μL of total RNA extract from brain tissue and AgPath-IDTM One-Step RT-PCR 118 reagents (Thermo Scientific) on a Bio-Rad CFX96 real-time PCR detection system. 119 Next Generation Sequencing 120 RNA extracted from the brain tissue specimen was quantified using the Qubit RNA HS Assay Kit 121 (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA, USA). A total of 100 ng of RNA from the sample was used 122 for library preparation with the Illumina RNA Prep with Enrichment (L) Tagmentation Kit (Cat. No. 123 20040536; Illumina, Inc., San Diego, CA, USA), which incorporates first- and second-strand cDNA 124 synthesis, tagmentation-based fragmentation, adapter/barcode ligation, and library amplification. 125 Target enrichment was performed using the Illumina Virus Surveillance Panel V2 (Cat. No. 20108081), 6 126 employing hybrid-capture enrichment probes for approximately 200 viral pathogens. The pooled, 127 enriched library was normalized to 10 pM and sequenced on the Illumina MiSeq platform using a MiSeq 128 Reagent Kit v3 (150 cycles; Cat. No. MS-102-3001), generating a total of 0.89 million paired-end reads 129 with a mean target coverage depth of 3368×. Raw FASTQ files (R1 and R2 reads) were processed using 130 the DRAGEN Microbial Enrichment analysis tool (Version 4.5.4000) on the Illumina BaseSpace 131 Sequencing Hub using default parameters. Sequence data have been deposited in the NCBI Sequence 132 Read Archive under accession number [submission in progress]. 133 Bioinformatics Analysis 134 Assembly and Annotation 135 Raw paired-end Illumina sequencing reads (2 × 76 bp) were assessed using FastQC (v0.12.1)(10) and 136 quality filtered using Fastp (v1.3.3)(11). This process included adapter trimming, a minimum Phred 137 quality score of 20, and a minimum post-trimming read length of 50 bp. The filtered reads were aligned 138 to the Arctic-Like 1a reference genome (GenBank accession PP737617; highest-quality complete 139 genome from the same lineage) using BWA-MEM (v0.7.17)(12) with default parameters. The 140 alignments were sorted and indexed using SAMtools (v1.20)(13), and variants were called using 141 BCFtools mpileup (v1.20; maximum depth = 1000) followed by BCFtools call (14). Consensus genome 142 sequences were generated using vcf2consensus.pl 143 (https://github.com/ellisrichardj/csu_scripts/tree/master) (15) with a minimum depth threshold of 20X; 144 positions below this threshold were masked as 'N'. Genome coverage, breadth of coverage, and 145 sequencing depth statistics were calculated from BAM alignment files using SAMtools coverage and 146 depth commands. Read mapping, variant calling, consensus sequence generation, and assembly quality 147 assessment were performed through a custom workflow incorporating the tools described above. 148 Lineage assignment of the novel sequence was performed using RABV-GLUE (16) and MADDOG 149 lineage-typing tool (17). 150 151 7 152 Sequence Retrieval 153 For phylogeographic analysis, a curated subset of RABV genomes was constructed based on established 154 lineage references. The initial dataset comprised 624 genomes in total, including 145 representative 155 Indian and regional sequences, 44 global lineage reference and outgroup sequences (Arctic AL1a–AL3, 156 AL2, Indian-Subcontinent, Cosmopolitan AF1a–AF4, and Asian SEA1–2 lineages) retrieved from the 157 RABV-GLUE database, and the novel genome generated in this study. To reduce redundancy, highly 158 similar genomes were clustered using CD-HIT (cd-hit-est) v4.8.1 (18) with a 99.5% nucleotide identity 159 threshold. One representative sequence per cluster was retained, yielding a non-redundant dataset of 86 160 genomes for downstream analysis. 161 Multiple Sequence Alignment 162 All 86 RABV genomes were aligned at the complete-genome level using MAFFT (v7.525) (19) with 163 the --auto strategy to automatically select the optimal algorithm. The resulting alignment was trimmed 164 using ClipKIT (v1.4.2) (20) in smart-gap mode to remove poorly aligned and highly gapped positions 165 while retaining phylogenetically informative sites. 166 Phylogenetic Reconstruction 167 Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis of the 86 genome dataset was executed using IQ-TREE 2 168 (v2.2.6, MPI version) (21). The best-fit nucleotide substitution model (GTR+F+R6) was selected using 169 ModelFinder; branch support was assessed using 1,000 ultrafast bootstrap replicates and used for 170 maximum-likelihood tree reconstruction. 171 t-SNE Clustering 172 To complement phylogenetic inference and visualize genome-wide genetic relationships among rabies 173 virus (RABV) isolates, t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE) was applied to a dataset of 174 600 complete, high-quality RABV reference genomes, independent of the phylogenetic dataset. 175 Pairwise genomic distances were first computed from the whole-genome alignment and used as input 176 for dimensionality reduction using the scikit-learn package (v1.3.0) in Python. The optimal number of 8 177 clusters was determined using the elbow method, followed by K-means clustering. Dimensionality 178 reduction and two-dimensional visualization were conducted using the scikit-learn package in Python 179 (v1.3.0) (22). 180 Mutation Analysis and Structural Alignment 181 Genomic variations in the novel study sequence were characterized through comparative mutational 182 analysis using an in-house Python script against the AL1a reference genome (GenBank: KF154996). 183 To evaluate the biological implications of non-synonymous substitutions, 3D structural alignments were 184 performed between predicted protein models of the isolate and corresponding wild-type structures using 185 the Protein Structure Alignment workflow in the Schrödinger suite. 186 Selection Pressure Analysis 187 The coding regions (CDS) of all five RABV proteins (G, M, N, P, and L) were analyzed for selection 188 pressure. Pervasive purifying and positive selection were determined using the Single-Likelihood 189 Ancestor Counting (SLAC) approach (23). The Mixed Effects Model of Evolution (MEME) (24) was 190 used to detect sites under positive (diversifying) selection. Both analyses were conducted using the 191 standard viral genetic code (translation table 11) with default settings and a significance threshold of p 192 ≤ 0.1 implemented in HyPhy through the Datamonkey web server (25). 193 Results 194 Detection of rabies virus antigen 195 Direct Fluorescent Antibody Test performed on acetone-fixed impression smears prepared from the 196 brain tissue specimen revealed strong positivity for rabies virus nucleoprotein antigen (Fig. 1), 197 confirming rabies encephalitis. 9 198 199 Fig 1. Direct Fluorescent Antibody Test on the brain tissue specimen, showing positivity for rabies 200 virus nucleoprotein antigen (punctate to diffuse bright apple-green fluorescence within cytoplasm and 201 neuronal processes) (420X). 202 203 Detection of rabies virus RNA 204 Real-time RT-PCR on total RNA extracted from brain tissue detected rabies virus RNA (mean cycle 205 threshold (Ct): 25.63 from duplicate wells). Successful co-amplification of the host beta-actin control 206 confirmed sample quality and RNA integrity. 207 High-Quality Reference-Based Genome Assembly and Lineage Annotation 208 Reference-guided assembly produced a complete genome sequence of 11,788 bp. The assembled 209 genome exhibited a GC content of 45.55% and contained no ambiguous nucleotides. The consensus 210 sequence achieved 100% genome coverage with a mean sequencing depth of 3,842.67X. Coverage was 211 uniformly distributed across the genome, with depths ranging from 43X to 9,187X. All genomic 10 212 positions were covered at depths ≥10×, while 99.96% and 99.90% of positions were covered at depths 213 ≥50× and ≥100×, respectively, indicating a high-confidence assembly suitable for downstream genomic 214 and phylogenetic analyses. The analysis using RABV-GLUE identified the virus as belonging to the 215 Arctic-like lineage 1a and further characterized it as the sub-lineage AL1a_A1.1. Independent 216 verification using MADDOG gave the same classification. According to the metadata, the AL1a_A1.1 217 sub-lineage was found only in India between 2003 and 2023. 218 Phylogenetic Analysis 219 For phylogenetic reconstruction, a curated, non-redundant dataset was generated by clustering 220 sequences with CD-HIT, yielding 86 representative genomes for tree inference. The multiple sequence 221 alignment was then trimmed…

papers.title: Laboratory-Based Surveillance of Animal Rabies in the Bono East Region of Ghana: A Six-Year Retrospective Study (2020 – 2025)
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Dog-mediated rabies remains a major neglected tropical disease and an important cause of preventable human mortality in sub-Saharan Africa. Despite ongoing control efforts, limited laboratory-confirmed surveillance data hinder accurate assessment of the disease burden and the development of evidence-based interventions in Ghana. This study investigated the epidemiological characteristics of laboratory-confirmed rabies cases among suspected animal submissions and evaluated the contribution of routine diagnostic surveillance to rabies control. Methodology/Principal Findings A retrospective analysis was conducted using laboratory surveillance records of suspected rabies cases submitted to a regional veterinary laboratory in Ghana between 2020 and 2025. Brain tissue samples were examined using Seller’s staining, the direct fluorescent antibody test (FAT), and polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Epidemiological information, including animal species, vaccination history, ownership status, bite history, and diagnostic outcomes, was extracted and analysed descriptively. Of the 51 suspected cases examined, 46 (90.2%) were laboratory confirmed as rabies. Domestic dogs accounted for 96.1% of submissions, while cats represented 3.9%. Most suspected animals were either unvaccinated (64.7%) or had unknown vaccination status (33.3%), and 90.2% had reportedly bitten humans before submission. Confirmed cases were detected throughout the study period, indicating sustained viral circulation and continued zoonotic risk within the study area. Conclusions/Significance The consistently high proportion of laboratory-confirmed rabies cases demonstrates persistent transmission of rabies virus among domestic animals and highlights substantial risks to human health. The integration of conventional and advanced laboratory diagnostic methods strengthened surveillance and improved case confirmation. These findings underscore the urgent need to expand dog vaccination coverage, strengthen laboratory-based surveillance, improve bite reporting systems, and enhance collaboration between veterinary and public health sectors. Reinforcing integrated One Health strategies will be essential to accelerate progress towards the global goal of eliminating dog-mediated human rabies by 2030. Author Summary Rabies remains one of the world’s oldest and most devastating zoonotic diseases, which is fatal yet preventable, causing thousands of human deaths each year, particularly in Africa and Asia. In Ghana, domestic dogs are the principal reservoir of the rabies virus, but information on the epidemiology of animal rabies from routine laboratory surveillance is limited in many regions. We reviewed six years (2020 – 2025) of laboratory records from the Regional Veterinary Laboratory in Techiman, Bono East Region, to describe the epidemiological characteristics of suspected animal rabies cases and laboratory-confirmed infections. Of the 51 brain samples submitted for diagnosis, 46 (90.2%) were confirmed positive for rabies. Domestic dogs accounted for almost all submissions, and most confirmed cases involved animals that were either unvaccinated or had an unknown vaccination history. Furthermore, most suspected animals had reportedly bitten humans before laboratory investigation, highlighting the continuing public health risk posed by canine rabies. The study also documents how regional diagnostic capacity was strengthened through collaboration with national reference laboratories, enabling the routine use of internationally recommended diagnostic methods such as the fluorescent antibody test and polymerase chain reaction. These findings provide valuable evidence to support enhanced rabies surveillance, increased mass dog vaccination, improved public awareness, and strengthened One Health collaboration. Such measures are essential for reducing human rabies deaths and supporting Ghana’s contribution to the global goal of eliminating dog-mediated human rabies by 2030.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要背景 狗介导的狂犬病仍然是一种被忽视的主要热带疾病,也是撒哈拉以南非洲地区可预防的人类死亡的一个重要原因。尽管加纳正在进行控制工作,但实验室确认的监测数据有限,阻碍了对疾病负担的准确评估和基于证据的干预措施的发展。本研究调查了疑似动物提交的实验室确诊狂犬病病例的流行病学特征,并评估了常规诊断监测对狂犬病控制的贡献。方法/主要结果 使用 2020 年至 2025 年间提交给加纳地区兽医实验室的疑似狂犬病病例的实验室监测记录进行回顾性分析。使用塞勒染色、直接荧光抗体测试 (FAT) 和聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 对脑组织样本进行检查。提取流行病学信息并进行描述性分析,包括动物种类、疫苗接种史、所有权状况、咬伤史和诊断结果。在检查的 51 例疑似病例中,46 例(90.2%)经实验室确诊为狂犬病。家养狗占提交内容的 96.1%,而猫则占 3.9%。大多数可疑动物要么未接种疫苗(64.7%),要么疫苗接种状况未知(33.3%),据报道,90.2%的动物在提交前曾咬伤过人类。在整个研究期间发现了确诊病例,表明研究区域内持续存在病毒传播和持续的人畜共患风险。结论/意义 实验室确诊的狂犬病病例比例持续较高,表明狂犬病病毒在家畜中持续传播,并凸显了对人类健康的重大风险。传统和先进实验室诊断方法的结合加强了监测并改善了病例确认。这些发现强调迫切需要扩大狗的疫苗接种覆盖范围、加强基于实验室的监测、改进咬伤报告系统以及加强兽医和公共卫生部门之间的合作。加强综合“同一个健康”战略对于加快实现到 2030 年消除由狗传播的人类狂犬病这一全球目标至关重要。作者摘要 狂犬病仍然是世界上最古老、最具破坏性的人畜共患疾病之一,这种疾病致命但可以预防,每年导致数千人死亡,特别是在非洲和亚洲。在加纳,家犬是狂犬病病毒的主要宿主,但许多地区的常规实验室监测提供的动物狂犬病流行病学信息有限。我们回顾了波诺东地区泰奇曼地区兽医实验室六年(2020 年至 2025 年)的实验室记录,以描述疑似动物狂犬病病例和实验室确诊感染的流行病学特征。在提交诊断的 51 份脑样本中,46 份(90.2%)被证实狂犬病呈阳性。家犬几乎占所有提交的病例,大多数确诊病例涉及未接种疫苗或疫苗接种史未知的动物。此外,据报道,大多数可疑动物在实验室调查之前就曾咬伤过人类,这凸显了犬类狂犬病对公共健康造成的持续风险。该研究还记录了如何通过与国家参考实验室合作加强区域诊断能力,从而能够常规使用国际推荐的诊断方法,例如荧光抗体测试和聚合酶链反应。这些发现为支持加强狂犬病监测、增加大规模狗疫苗接种、提高公众意识和加强“同一个健康”合作提供了宝贵的证据。这些措施对于减少人类狂犬病死亡和支持加纳为到 2030 年消除由狗传播的人类狂犬病全球目标做出贡献至关重要。

papers.title: CAMKV is an ISG and facilitates the degradation of rabies virus phosphoprotein via SQSTM1-mediated selective autophagy
papers.abstract: Once rabies virus (RABV) gains access to the central nervous system, infection almost inevitably results in fatal outcomes, and our incomplete understanding of viral pathogenesis remains a major barrier to effective therapeutic intervention. Here, we identify CAMKV as an interferon-stimulated gene (ISG) that drives the macroautophagic/autophagic degradation of RABV phosphoprotein (P), thereby potently suppressing viral replication in vitro. Notably, in vivo overexpression of CAMKV significantly delays disease progression in mice challenged with a street strain of RABV. papers.title: Regulatory role of noncoding RNAs in infections caused by Rhabdoviridae family viruses
papers.abstract: The Rhabdoviridae family comprises negative-sense single-stranded RNA viruses that cause severe infections in a wide range of hosts. Increasing evidence indicates that host noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs), including microRNAs (miRNAs), long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs), and circular RNAs (circRNAs), play central roles in regulating rhabdovirus replication, pathogenesis, and host immune responses. These ncRNAs exert both antiviral and proviral effects through modulation of innate immune signaling pathways, regulation of gene expression, and control of inflammatory responses. Antiviral ncRNAs suppress viral replication by promoting interferon production and interferon-stimulated genes and by activating inflammatory and antiviral defense pathways. On the other hand, proviral ncRNAs facilitate viral survival and replication through modulation or inhibition of key signaling pathways such as NF-κB and JAK/STAT. This review provides a pathway-centric synthesis of ncRNA-mediated regulatory mechanisms in rhabdovirus infections, with particular emphasis on Chandipura virus, vesicular stomatitis virus, and rabies virus. By integrating current findings on the cellular and molecular interactions between ncRNAs and rhabdoviruses, this review highlights the dual regulatory roles of ncRNAs in viral pathogenesis and host immunity and discusses their potential as therapeutic targets and biomarkers for the control of rhabdoviral infections.

papers.title: Rabies and emerging infections: a one health review of the oldest zoonosis in an age of new spillovers
papers.abstract: On 6 July 1885, Louis Pasteur administered the first rabies vaccine to a bitten child, a moment now commemorated annually as World Zoonoses Day. Almost a century and a half later, rabies endures as the most lethal zoonosis known to medicine, claiming an estimated fifty-nine thousand human lives every year despite being entirely vaccine-preventable. This review uses rabies as a lens through which to examine the broader landscape of emerging and re-emerging infections that arise at the animal–human–environment interface. We trace the biology of the rabies virus and its relatives within the genus Lyssavirus, the mechanisms by which the virus invades the nervous system, and the clinical and laboratory features that define the disease. We then summarise the global and Indian burden, the modern pillars of prevention—wound care, post-exposure prophylaxis, mass dog vaccination, the emerging use of oral vaccines and integrated surveillance—and the World Health Organization’s “Zero by 30” goal that India has adopted through its National Action Plan for Dog Mediated Rabies Elimination. Turning outward, we ask why the majority of newly emerging human pathogens originate in animals, and we consider the ecological and socio-economic drivers of spillover through detailed examples including highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1, Nipah virus, SARS-CoV-2 and mpox. Throughout, we argue that the One Health framework is the connective tissue linking the elimination of an ancient disease to preparedness for novel outbreaks, and that veterinarians, positioned at this interface, are indispensable to both endeavours.
authors: Mervin Kennady R.V.,Thirumurthi K., Veeramalla Divya, Dimalie Michui

papers.title: Profile of Rabies Vaccination Administration for Patients Bitten by Dogs at the Natarandang Community Health Centre, Wolomeze Sub-district, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia
papers.abstract: Introduction: Rabies is a viral disease that is almost always fatal once clinical symptoms appear, with dogs being the primary source of transmission. This study aims to describe the rabies vaccination profile of dog bite patients at Natarandang Health Center, Wolomeze District. Methods: A retrospective descriptive study on 32 patients who received rabies vaccination after dog bites between January 2022 and February 2023. Data were collected from medical records and analyzed descriptively. Results: Most patients were male (65.6%), with the most common bite locations in the calf (34.4%) and hand (28.1%). The most frequent first aid measures included checking the dog's infection history and seeking medical attention (34.4% each). The most commonly administered rabies vaccine was PCECV (81.3%). Delayed medical care was associated with fever (65.6%) as the predominant symptom. Conclusion: Most dog bite patients at Natarandang Health Center were male, with the most common bite locations in the calf and hand. The most frequently reported first aid were checking the dog’s history and seeking medical attention. The predominant rabies vaccine administered was PCECV. Fever was the most common symptom.

papers.title_zh: 印度尼西亚东努沙登加拉省沃洛梅泽分区 Natarandang 社区卫生中心为被狗咬伤的患者注射狂犬病疫苗的情况
papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Rabies is a viral disease that is almost always fatal once clinical symptoms appear, with dogs being the primary source of transmission. This study aims to describe the rabies vaccination profile of dog bite patients at Natarandang Health Center, Wolomeze District. Methods: A retrospective descriptive study on 32 patients who received rabies vaccination after dog bites between January 2022 and February 2023. Data were collected from medical records and analyzed descriptively. Results: Most patients were male (65.6%), with the most common bite locations in the calf (34.4%) and hand (28.1%). The most frequent first aid measures included checking the dog's infection history and seeking medical attention (34.4% each). The most commonly administered rabies vaccine was PCECV (81.3%). Delayed medical care was associated with fever (65.6%) as the predominant symptom. Conclusion: Most dog bite patients at Natarandang Health Center were male, with the most common bite locations in the calf and hand. The most frequently reported first aid were checking the dog’s history and seeking medical attention. The predominant rabies vaccine administered was PCECV. Fever was the most common symptom.
papers.abstract_zh: 简介:狂犬病是一种病毒性疾病,一旦出现临床症状,几乎总是致命的,而狗是主要传播源。本研究旨在描述沃洛梅兹区 Natarandang 健康中心被狗咬伤的患者的狂犬病疫苗接种情况。方法:对 2022 年 1 月至 2023 年 2 月期间 32 名被狗咬伤后接受狂犬病疫苗接种的患者进行回顾性描述性研究。从病历中收集数据并进行描述性分析。结果:大多数患者为男性(65.6%),最常见的咬伤部位为小腿(34.4%)和手(28.1%)。最常见的急救措施包括检查狗的感染史和就医(各占34.4%)。最常用的狂犬病疫苗是 PCECV(81.3%)。延误医疗护理与发烧(65.6%)为主要症状有关。结论:Natarandang 健康中心的狗咬伤患者大多数为男性,最常见的咬伤部位是小腿和手部。最常报告的急救方法是检查狗的病史并寻求医疗救助。主要接种的狂犬病疫苗是 PCECV。发烧是最常见的症状。

papers.abstract: Dataset for "Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics for high-throughput reconstruction of neural circuits"This repository contains preprocessed data for "Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics for high-throughput reconstruction of neural circuits" by A. Becalick, A. Blot, M. Strom, and P. Znamenskiy.The code required to reproduce the analyses is available at https://github.com/znamlab/brisc.The archive contains a config file and 5 subfolders:barcode_diversity_analysis: sequencing data from viral and plasmid librariesrabies_barcoding: serial two-photon tomography and confocal databecalia_iss_microscope: microscope calibrationccf_streamlines: data from Allen CCF streamlines for conversion of cell locations to cortical flatmap coordinatesbecalia_rabies_barseq: in situ sequencing databarcode_diversity_analysisThe sequencing data are provided in the collapsed_barcode subfolder, which contains a subfolder for each library. Each subfolder contains one text file with number of UMI count and the sequence for each barcode.rabies_barcodingThe serial two-photon tomography and confocal data for the PhP.eB dilution experiments and the rabies bulk labeling are organised with a folder per mouse.Mice starting with BRJN are the Ai14 tdTomato reporter mice used for the PHP.eB dilution experiments. mice_list.csv contains a summary of experimental conditions for this experiment. Each mouse folder contains a cellfinder_results subfolder with the registered Allen CCF atlas (at 25 um voxel resolution, in the registration folder) and the detected cells (in the points folder).BRYC64.2h is the mouse used for bulk rabies tracing (Fig1 h-j). It contains the cellfinder data, organised as described above and an example confocal image in the zeiss_confocal folder.tail_vs_local contains data for the comparison of intracortical and intravenous delivery of Cre, including tiff files of the injection site of the two mice and the manually determined position of cells in an xml file.becalia_iss_microscopeContains calibration data of the microscope including a dark frame image in becalia_iss_microscope/calibration/cellcam_dark_frame_2024_02_06/cellcam_dark_frame_2024_02_06_MMStack_Pos0.ome.tif for image offset estimation.ccf_streamlinesContains the Allen CCF streamlines used for conversion of cell locations to cortical flatmap coordinates obtained from https://ccf-streamlines.readthedocs.io/en/latest/data_files.html.becalia_rabies_barseqContains the in situ sequencing data. The main in situ sequencing is in the BRAC8498.3e folder. Positions of the serial sections are detailed in section_position.csv. BRAC8498.3e/analysis contains the processed data including:adata_q.h5ad: an AnnData dataset of gene expression of all cellsBRAC8498.3e_error_corrected_barcodes_26_cell_barcode_df.pkl: a pandas DataFrame containing barcode information for all cellsBRAC8498.3e_error_corrected_barcodes_26_in_situ_barcodes.pkl and BRAC8498.3e_error_corrected_barcodes_26_random_barcodes.pkl: contain the matches between the plasmid library and the barcode detected in situ or random barcodes, respectively. They can be regenerated using match_to_library.py in https://github.com/znamlab/brisc.analysis/mcherry_cells: contains the position of. manually detected mCherry cells for the non-sequenced flow cell (chamber_06)analysis/starter_cells: contains pandas DataFrames with position and fluorescence information of starter cellschamber_XX: data for the 4 sequenced flow cells in individual folders, containing a pandas DataFrame with the barcode spot information (barcode_round_spots_1.pkl), the positions of detected mCherry cells (cells/mCherry_1_cells/mCherry_1_df_corrected_curated.pkl) and registration to the Allen CCF for each ROI (register_to_ara), including a metadata file per ROI, the x,y,z coordinates of each pixel in the CCF as multichannel tiff file (ara_coordinates) and the area ID for each pixel (area_images). For chamber_08 only, example raw data from one tile can be found in the barcode_round_X_1 and genes_round_X_1 folders (where X is the sequencing round number).BRAC8780.3f: data for the sensitivity analysis of Figure 3e. It contains data from one flow cell (chamber_08) including raw data of the hybridisation round (hybridisation_round_1_1) as well as registration information (reg) and metadata.

Dataset for "Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics for high-throughput reconstruction of neural circuits" dataset posted on 2026-07-16, 13:55 authored by Petr ZnamenskiyPetr Znamenskiy, Alexander BecalickAlexander Becalick, Antonin BlotAntonin Blot, Molly StromMolly Strom

Dataset for "Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics for high-throughput reconstruction of neural circuits"

This repository contains preprocessed data for "Barcoded Rabies In Situ Connectomics for high-throughput reconstruction of neural circuits" by A. Becalick, A. Blot, M. Strom, and P. Znamenskiy.

The code required to reproduce the analyses is available at https://github.com/znamlab/brisc.

The archive contains a config file and 5 subfolders:

  • barcode_diversity_analysis: sequencing data from viral and plasmid libraries
  • rabies_barcoding: serial two-photon tomography and confocal data
  • becalia_iss_microscope: microscope calibration
  • ccf_streamlines: data from Allen CCF streamlines for conversion of cell locations to cortical flatmap coordinates
  • becalia_rabies_barseq: in situ sequencing data

barcode_diversity_analysis

The sequencing data are provided in the collapsed_barcode subfolder, which contains a subfolder for each library. Each subfolder contains one text file with number of UMI count and the sequence for each barcode.

rabies_barcoding

The serial two-photon tomography and confocal data for the PhP.eB dilution experiments and the rabies bulk labeling are organised with a folder per mouse.

  • Mice starting with BRJN are the Ai14 tdTomato reporter mice used for the PHP.eB dilution experiments. mice_list.csv contains a summary of experimental conditions for this experiment. Each mouse folder contains a cellfinder_results subfolder with the registered Allen CCF atlas (at 25 um voxel resolution, in the registration folder) and the detected cells (in the points folder).
  • BRYC64.2h is the mouse used for bulk rabies tracing (Fig1 h-j). It contains the cellfinder data, organised as described above and an example confocal image in the zeiss_confocal folder.
  • tail_vs_local contains data for the comparison of intracortical and intravenous delivery of Cre, including tiff files of the injection site of the two mice and the manually determined position of cells in an xml file.

becalia_iss_microscope

Contains calibration data of the microscope including a dark frame image in becalia_iss_microscope/calibration/cellcam_dark_frame_2024_02_06/cellcam_dark_frame_2024_02_06_MMStack_Pos0.ome.tif for image offset estimation.

ccf_streamlines

Contains the Allen CCF streamlines used for conversion of cell locations to cortical flatmap coordinates obtained from https://ccf-streamlines.readthedocs.io/en/latest/data_files.html.

becalia_rabies_barseq

Contains the in situ sequencing data. The main in situ sequencing is in the BRAC8498.3e folder. Positions of the serial sections are detailed in section_position.csv. BRAC8498.3e/analysis contains the processed data including:

  • adata_q.h5ad: an AnnData dataset of gene expression of all cells
  • BRAC8498.3e_error_corrected_barcodes_26_cell_barcode_df.pkl: a pandas DataFrame containing barcode information for all cells
  • BRAC8498.3e_error_corrected_barcodes_26_in_situ_barcodes.pkl and BRAC8498.3e_error_corrected_barcodes_26_random_barcodes.pkl: contain the matches between the plasmid library and the barcode detected in situ or random barcodes, respectively. They can be regenerated using match_to_library.py in https://github.com/znamlab/brisc.
  • analysis/mcherry_cells: contains the position of. manually detected mCherry cells for the non-sequenced flow cell (chamber_06)
  • analysis/starter_cells: contains pandas DataFrames with position and fluorescence information of starter cells
  • chamber_XX: data for the 4 sequenced flow cells in individual folders, containing a pandas DataFrame with the barcode spot information (barcode_round_spots_1.pkl), the positions of detected mCherry cells (cells/mCherry_1_cells/mCherry_1_df_corrected_curated.pkl) and registration to the Allen CCF for each ROI (register_to_ara), including a metadata file per ROI, the x,y,z coordinates of each pixel in the CCF as multichannel tiff file (ara_coordinates) and the area ID for each pixel (area_images). For chamber_08 only, example raw data from one tile can be found in the barcode_round_X_1 and genes_round_X_1 folders (where X is the sequencing round number).
  • BRAC8780.3f: data for the sensitivity analysis of Figure 3e. It contains data from one flow cell (chamber_08) including raw data of the hybridisation round (hybridisation_round_1_1) as well as registration information (reg) and metadata.

Funding History Related Materials - 1.

  • tail_vs_local contains data for the comparison of intracortical and intravenous delivery of Cre, including tiff files of the injection site of the two mice and the manually determined position of cells in an xml file.

becalia_iss_microscope

Contains calibration data of the microscope including a dark frame image in becalia_iss_microscope/calibration/cellcam_dark_frame_2024_02_06/cellcam_dark_frame_2024_02_06_MMStack_Pos0.ome.tif for image offset estimation.

ccf_streamlines

Contains the Allen CCF streamlines used for conversion of cell locations to cortical flatmap coordinates obtained from https://ccf-streamlines.readthedocs.io/en/latest/data_files.html.

becalia_rabies_barseq

Contains the in situ sequencing data. The main in situ sequencing is in the BRAC8498.3e folder. Positions of the serial sections are detailed in section_position.csv. BRAC8498.3e/analysis contains the processed data including:

  • adata_q.h5ad: an AnnData dataset of gene expression of all cells
  • BRAC8498.3e_error_corrected_barcodes_26_cell_barcode_df.pkl: a pandas DataFrame containing barcode information for all cells
  • BRAC8498.3e_error_corrected_barcodes_26_in_situ_barcodes.pkl and BRAC8498.3e_error_corrected_barcodes_26_random_barcodes.pkl: contain the matches between the plasmid library and the barcode detected in situ or random barcodes, respectively. They can be regenerated using match_to_library.py in https://github.com/znamlab/brisc.
  • analysis/mcherry_cells: contains the position of. manually detected mCherry cells for the non-sequenced flow cell (chamber_06)
  • analysis/starter_cells: contains pandas DataFrames with position and fluorescence information of starter cells
  • chamber_XX: data for the 4 sequenced flow cells in individual folders, containing a pandas DataFrame with the barcode spot information (barcode_round_spots_1.pkl), the positions of detected mCherry cells (cells/mCherry_1_cells/mCherry_1_df_corrected_curated.pkl) and registration to the Allen CCF for each ROI (register_to_ara), including a metadata file per ROI, the x,y,z coordinates of each pixel in the CCF as multichannel tiff file (ara_coordinates) and the area ID for each pixel (area_images). For chamber_08 only, example raw data from one tile can be found in the barcode_round_X_1 and genes_round_X_1 folders (where X is the sequencing round number).
  • BRAC8780.3f: data for the sensitivity analysis of Figure 3e. It contains data from one flow cell (chamber_08) including raw data of the hybridisation round (hybridisation_round_1_1) as well as registration information (reg) and metadata.

papers.abstract_zh: “用于高通量重建神经回路的条形码狂犬病原位连接组学”的数据集此存储库包含 A. Znamenskiy 的“用于高通量神经回路重建的条形码狂犬病原位连接组学”的预处理数据。重现分析所需的代码可在 https://github.com/znamlab/brisc 上找到。存档包含一个配置文件和 5 个文件。子文件夹:barcode_diversity_analysis:来自病毒和质粒文库的测序数据rabies_barcoding:串行双光子断层扫描和共焦数据becalia_iss_microscope:显微镜校准ccf_streamlines:来自 Allen CCF 流线的数据,用于将细胞位置转换为皮质平面图坐标becalia_rabies_barseq:原位测序数据barcode_diversity_analysis测序数据在collapsed_barcode子文件夹中提供,其中包含每个库的子文件夹。每个子文件夹包含一个文本文件,其中包含 UMI 计数数量和每个条形码的序列。rabies_barcodingPhP.eB 稀释实验和狂犬病批量标记的串行双光子断层扫描和共聚焦数据按每只小鼠的一个文件夹进行组织。以 BRJN 开头的小鼠是用于 PHP.eB 稀释的 Ai14 tdTomato 报告小鼠实验。mice_list.csv 包含此实验的实验条件摘要。每个鼠标文件夹都包含一个 cellfinder_results 子文件夹,其中包含注册的 Allen CCF 图集(在注册文件夹中,25 um 体素分辨率)和检测到的细胞(在点文件夹中)。BRYC64.2h 是用于批量狂犬病追踪的鼠标(图 1 h-j)。它包含按上述方式组织的 cellfinder 数据以及 zeiss_confocal 文件夹中的示例共焦图像。tail_vs_local包含用于比较皮质内和静脉注射 Cre 的数据,包括两只小鼠注射部位的 tiff 文件以及 xml 文件中手动确定的细胞位置。becalia_iss_microscope包含显微镜在 becalia_iss_microscope/calibration/cellcam_dark_frame_2024_02_06/cellcam_dark_frame_2024_02_06_MMStack_Pos0.ome.tif 中包含暗帧图像,用于图像偏移估计。ccf_streamlines包含用于转换细胞的 Allen CCF 流线从 https://ccf-streamlines.readthedocs.io/en/latest/data_files.html 获取的皮质平面坐标位置。becalia_rabies_barseq包含原位测序数据。主要的原位测序位于 BRAC8498.3e 文件夹中。section_position.csv 中详细介绍了串行部分的位置。BRAC8498.3e/analysis 包含处理后的数据,包括:adata_q.h5ad:所有细胞基因表达的 AnnData 数据集BRAC8498.3e_error_ Corrected_barcodes_26_cell_barcode_df.pkl:包含所有细胞条形码信息的 pandas DataFrame cellsBRAC8498.3e_error_ Corrected_barcodes_26_in_situ_barcodes.pkl 和BRAC8498.3e_error_ Corrected_barcodes_26_random_barcodes.pkl:包含质粒库与原位或随机检测到的条形码之间的匹配分别是条形码。它们可以使用 https://github.com/znamlab/brisc 中的 ma​​tch_to_library.py 重新生成。analysis/mcherry_cells:包含 的位置。手动检测到的非测序流动槽 (chamber_06) 的 mCherry 细胞analysis/starter_cells:包含带有起始细胞位置和荧光信息的 pandas DataFramechamber_XX:各个文件夹中 4 个测序流动槽的数据,包含带有条形码点信息的 pandas DataFrame (barcode_round_spots_1.pkl)、检测到的 mCherry 细胞的位置 (cells/mCherry_1_cells/mCherry_1_df_ Corrected_curated.pkl) 以及每个 ROI 的 Allen CCF 注册 (register_to_ara),包括每个 ROI 的元数据文件ROI、多通道 tiff 文件形式的 CCF 中每个像素的 x、y、z 坐标 (ara_coordinates) 以及每个像素的区域 ID (area_images)。仅对于 chamber_08,来自一个图块的示例原始数据可以在 barcode_round_X_1 和 genes_round_X_1 文件夹中找到(其中 X 是测序轮数)。BRAC8780.3f:用于图 3e 敏感性分析的数据。它包含来自一个流动槽 (chamber_08) 的数据,包括杂交轮次的原始数据 (hybridization_round_1_1) 以及注册信息 (reg) 和元数据。

papers.title: A scoping review of One Health interventions 2005–2025: What has been done, are they effective, and what are the best practices?
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: One Health research and practice are evolving rapidly, necessitating solid evidence-building and quality assessment of One Health interventions. We conducted a scoping review to (1) characterize how many and what kinds of One Health interventions are published in peer-reviewed literature; and (2) assess whether the identified interventions demonstrated effectiveness. We hypothesized that the evidence was limited in numbers and ability to demonstrate effectiveness. METHODS: The review was reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews. The initial search was conducted on Medline (Ovid), Embase, PubAg, and Web of Science in May 2024 and updated in December 2025. Inclusion criteria were: Primary research in which the investigators intervened with humans, animals, or their shared environment (at least two of three domains); an outcome assessment was included, and full text was available in English, published on or before December 16, 2025. Two researchers independently screened and analyzed all manuscripts. RESULTS: Over 18,000 references were screened, and 151 studies were included. Studies were conducted in 53 countries representing all six WHO Regions. The highest number of interventions were reported from the United States of America, Tanzania, and India. Among 79 interventions that targeted zoonoses, the most common diseases were general zoonoses, rabies, and cysticercosis. Over half (55%) of the study designs were quasi-experimental, followed by 23% randomized control trials (RCTs) and 19% non-randomized experiments. Less than half (41%) of the studies had a control or comparison group. The most common perceived sources of bias were immigrative (28%) and emigrative selection bias (11%). Eight field-based RCTs identified that a One Health intervention was effective in reducing disease occurrence or pathogen detection compared to the control. Exemplary practices included a comprehensive intervention spanning human, animal, and environmental domains, using a participatory approach, assessing longer-term outcomes, triangulating results using more than one method, not overstating findings, and providing a visual aid to describe the intervention. CONCLUSIONS: A small number of field-based RCTs clearly demonstrated the comparative effectiveness of One Health interventions, while it was challenging to assess the effectiveness of other studies without a more granular definition of effectiveness. Rigorous studies that assess the effectiveness of One Health interventions will collectively improve buy-in from governments, researchers, and policymakers, and advance the evidence base for employing the One Health approach.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines One Health interventions across human, animal, and environmental domains, focusing on their characterization and effectiveness assessment within peer-reviewed literature from 2005 to 2025. The central question addresses what types of One Health interventions exist and whether they demonstrate effectiveness in reducing disease occurrence or pathogen detection.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This scoping review followed PRISMA-ScR guidelines and searched Medline (Ovid), Embase, PubAg, and Web of Science in May 2024, updated in December 2025. Inclusion criteria required primary research with interventions spanning at least two of three One Health domains, outcome assessment, and full-text availability in English, published by December 16, 2025. Two independent researchers screened and analyzed manuscripts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Eight field-based randomized controlled trials (RCTs) demonstrated that One Health interventions effectively reduced disease occurrence or pathogen detection compared to controls. Exemplary practices included comprehensive multi-domain interventions, participatory approaches, longer-term outcome assessment, triangulation of methods, cautious interpretation of findings, and visual aids to describe interventions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Less than half (41%) of studies included a control or comparison group, and quasi-experimental designs dominated (55%), limiting causal inference. Selection bias, particularly immigrative (28%) and emigrative (11%), was frequently identified. The review highlights a lack of granular definitions for effectiveness, complicating assessments beyond field-based RCTs.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize rigorous study designs with control groups to strengthen causal evidence. Standardizing definitions of effectiveness and incorporating longer-term outcomes and triangulation methods are critical. Addressing selection bias and expanding multi-domain interventions can enhance policy relevance and stakeholder buy-in.

analysis.summary_en: This scoping review evaluates One Health interventions published between 2005 and 2025, focusing on their characterization and effectiveness. Using PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the review screened over 18,000 references and included 151 studies from 53 countries, with the highest number of interventions reported in the USA, Tanzania, and India. Among 79 zoonotic interventions, rabies and cysticercosis were most common. Only eight field-based RCTs demonstrated effectiveness in reducing disease or pathogen detection, while quasi-experimental designs (55%) and limited control groups (41%) constrained causal inference. Selection bias, particularly immigrative (28%) and emigrative (11%), was prevalent. The review underscores the need for standardized effectiveness definitions, rigorous designs, and multi-domain approaches to strengthen evidence and policy impact.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:“同一个健康”研究和实践正在迅速发展,需要对“同一个健康”干预措施建立可靠的证据和质量评估。我们进行了范围界定审查,目的是 (1) 描述同行评审文献中发表的 One Health 干预措施的数量和类型;(2) 评估所确定的干预措施是否有效。我们假设证据的数量和证明有效性的能力有限。方法:根据系统评价的首选报告项目和范围界定评价的荟萃分析扩展来报告评价。最初的检索于 2024 年 5 月在 Medline (Ovid)、Embase、PubAg 和 Web of Science 上进行,并于 2025 年 12 月更新。纳入标准为: 研究人员干预人类、动物或其共享环境(三个领域中的至少两个)的主要研究;其中包括结果评估,全文有英文版,于 2025 年 12 月 16 日或之前发表。两名研究人员独立筛选和分析了所有手稿。结果:筛选了超过 18,000 篇参考文献,纳入了 151 项研究。研究在代表世卫组织所有六个区域的 53 个国家进行。据报告,美国、坦桑尼亚和印度的干预次数最多。在 79 项针对人畜共患疾病的干预措施中,最常见的疾病是一般人畜共患病、狂犬病和囊虫病。超过一半 (55%) 的研究设计是准实验性的,其次是 23% 的随机对照试验 (RCT) 和 19% 的非随机实验。不到一半 (41%) 的研究设有对照组。最常见的偏见来源是移民(28%)和移民选择偏见(11%)。八项基于现场的随机对照试验表明,与对照相比,“同一个健康”干预措施可有效减少疾病发生或病原体检测。典型的实践包括跨越人类、动物和环境领域的综合干预,使用参与式方法,评估长期结果,使用多种方法对结果进行三角测量,不夸大发现,并提供视觉辅助来描述干预措施。结论:少数实地随机对照试验清楚地证明了“同一个健康”干预措施的相对有效性,而在没有更细粒度的有效性定义的情况下,评估其他研究的有效性具有挑战性。评估“同一个健康”干预措施有效性的严格研究将共同​​提高政府、研究人员和政策制定者的支持度,并推进采用“同一个健康”方法的证据基础。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述审查了人类、动物和环境领域的“同一个健康”干预措施,重点关注 2005 年至 2025 年同行评审文献中的特征和有效性评估。核心问题是存在哪些类型的“同一个健康”干预措施,以及它们是否在减少疾病发生或病原体检测方面表现出有效性。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本次范围界定审查遵循 PRISMA-ScR 指南,并于 2024 年 5 月检索了 Medline (Ovid)、Embase、PubAg 和 Web of Science,并于 2025 年 12 月更新。纳入标准要求进行初步研究,干预措施至少涵盖三个 One Health 领域中的两个、结果评估和英文全文,于 2025 年 12 月 16 日出版。两名独立研究人员筛选和分析了手稿。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 八项实地随机对照试验 (RCT) 表明,与对照相比,One Health 干预措施有效减少了疾病发生或病原体检测。典型的做法包括全面的多领域干预措施、参与性方法、长期结果评估、方法三角测量、对结果的谨慎解释以及描述干预措施的视觉辅助工具。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 不到一半 (41%) 的研究包括对照组或比较组,并且准实验设计占主导地位 (55%),限制了因果推断。选择偏差,特别是移民(28%)和移民(11%),经常被发现。该审查强调缺乏有效性的细化定义,使实地随机对照试验之外的评估变得复杂。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 未来的研究应优先考虑与对照组进行严格的研究设计,以加强因果证据。标准化有效性定义并纳入长期结果和三角测量方法至关重要。解决选择偏差和扩大多领域干预措施可以增强政策相关性和利益相关者的支持。

papers.title: World Zoonoses Day 2026: Community Action Through One Health Is the Foundation for Preventing Future Outbreaks
papers.abstract: World Zoonoses Day: A Global Call for Collective Responsibility Every year on 6 July, the global community observes World Zoonoses Day to commemorate a landmark event in the history of preventive medicine. On this day in 1885, Louis Pasteur successfully administered the first rabies vaccine to a young boy bitten by a rabid dog, demonstrating that scientific innovation could prevent one of the world's most feared infectious diseases. More than a century later, the significance of this achievement extends far beyond rabies. It symbolizes humanity's continuing struggle against zoonotic diseases—those infections that circulate at the interface of humans, animals and the environment.
authors: Dr. Nidhi Rawat, Dr. C. Sannat, Dr. Nitin E. Gade and Dr. Jasmeet Singh

papers.title: RVG-functionalized microglial membrane–coated cerium–gallic acid metal–organic frameworks for multi-target Alzheimer's therapy
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder characterized by aberrant β-amyloid (Aβ) aggregation, oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and disrupted metal ion homeostasis, which limit the efficacy of conventional single-target therapies. To address these intertwined pathological processes, we developed a multifunctional nanotherapeutic platform based on a cerium-gallic acid bio-metal-organic framework (CeGA-MOF). Reversible Ce3+/Ce4+ redox cycling enables efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging, while gallic acid serves as both an organic ligand and metal chelator, inhibiting metal ion-mediated Aβ aggregation and alleviating oxidative stress-associated neurotoxicity, along with its intrinsic anti-inflammatory activity. To enhance in vivo stability and brain delivery, CeGA-MOF was coated with microglial membranes and functionalized with rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG) peptide, yielding a biomimetic nanosystem, CeGA-MOF/B/R. The microglial membrane provides immune evasion and inflammation-guided targeting, while RVG facilitates blood-brain barrier penetration. In vitro, CeGA-MOF/B/R effectively chelates Cu2+, Zn2+, and Fe3+, suppresses metal ion-induced Aβ aggregation, and protects neurons. In APP/PS1 transgenic mice, it reduced cerebral Aβ, promoted anti-inflammatory microglial polarization, and improved learning and memory, highlighting its potential as a biomimetic nanoplatform for synergistic AD therapy.
papers.journal: Journal of Colloid and Interface Science

To address these intertwined pathological processes, we developed a multifunctional nanotherapeutic platform based on a cerium-gallic acid bio-metal-organic framework (CeGA-MOF). Reversible Ce3+/Ce4+ redox cycling enables efficient reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging, while gallic acid serves as both an organic ligand and metal chelator, inhibiting metal ion-mediated Aβ aggregation and alleviating oxidative stress-associated neurotoxicity, along with its intrinsic anti-inflammatory activity. To enhance in vivo stability and brain delivery, CeGA-MOF was coated with microglial membranes and functionalized with rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG) peptide, yielding a biomimetic nanosystem, CeGA-MOF/B/R. The microglial membrane provides immune evasion and inflammation-guided targeting, while RVG facilitates blood-brain barrier penetration. In vitro, CeGA-MOF/B/R effectively chelates Cu2+, Zn2+, and Fe3+, suppresses metal ion-induced Aβ aggregation, and protects neurons. In APP/PS1 transgenic mice, it reduced cerebral Aβ, promoted anti-inflammatory microglial polarization, and improved learning and memory, highlighting its potential as a biomimetic nanoplatform for synergistic AD therapy.

papers.abstract_zh: 阿尔茨海默病(AD)是一种多因素神经退行性疾病,其特征是异常的β-淀粉样蛋白(Aβ)聚集、氧化应激、神经炎症和金属离子稳态破坏,这些限制了传统单靶点疗法的疗效。为了解决这些相互交织的病理过程,我们开发了一种基于铈没食子酸生物金属有机框架(CeGA-MOF)的多功能纳米治疗平台。可逆的 Ce3+/Ce4+ 氧化还原循环能够有效清除活性氧 (ROS),而没食子酸既可以作为有机配体,也可以作为金属螯合剂,抑制金属离子介导的 Aβ 聚集,减轻氧化应激相关的神经毒性,并具有内在的抗炎活性。为了增强体内稳定性和脑输送,CeGA-MOF 涂有小胶质细胞膜,并用狂犬病病毒糖蛋白 (RVG) 肽进行功能化,产生仿生纳米系统 CeGA-MOF/B/R。小胶质细胞膜提供免疫逃避和炎症引导的靶向,而 RVG 则促进血脑屏障穿透。在体外,CeGA-MOF/B/R 有效螯合 Cu2+、Zn2+ 和 Fe3+,抑制金属离子诱导的 Aβ 聚集,并保护神经元。在 APP/PS1 转基因小鼠中,它减少了大脑 Aβ,促进抗炎小胶质细胞极化,并改善学习和记忆,凸显了其作为协同 AD 治疗的仿生纳米平台的潜力。

papers.title: Alphavirus madariaga-associated encephalomyelitis in equines from the Brazilian Pantanal reveals arbovirus circulation in a peri-urban environment
papers.abstract: Alphavirus madariaga (MADV), a member of the eastern equine encephalitis virus complex, is an emerging arbovirus in South America, with limited information regarding its occurrence and molecular characterization in equine populations. This study reports the detection and genetic characterization of MADV in equines from the state of Mato Grosso, Brazil. Two horses presenting acute neurological disease with a clinical course of approximately two days were evaluated. Histopathological examination revealed nonsuppurative meningoencephalomyelitis. Molecular screening for neurotropic viruses using TaqMan RT-qPCR assays was negative for rabies virus, EHV-1, WEEV, VEEV, WNV, and flaviviruses, while MADV was detected with Ct values of 27.9 and 31.4. Partial NS1 and E1 gene fragments were amplified and sequenced. Phylogenetic analyses based on both genes consistently placed the strain, named Santo Antonio, within the MADV genotype III clade, with strong support in the E1 analysis. The cases occurred in a peri-urban area located near Santo Antônio do Leverger, approximately 30 km from Cuiabá, highlighting a potential interface between sylvatic and human-modified environments. These findings provide molecular evidence of MADV circulation in central-western Brazil and association with equines disease. Our results reinforce the role of horses as sentinels for neurotropic arbovirus surveillance before reaching human population.
papers.journal: Comparative Immunology Microbiology and Infectious Diseases

papers.abstract_zh: 马达里亚加甲病毒 (MADV) 是东部马脑炎病毒复合体的成员,是南美洲一种新兴的虫媒病毒,有关其在马群体中的发生和分子特征的信息有限。本研究报告了巴西马托格罗索州马科动物 MADV 的检测和遗传特征。对两匹患有急性神经系统疾病、临床病程大约为两天的马进行了评估。组织病理学检查显示非化脓性脑膜脑脊髓炎。使用 TaqMan RT-qPCR 检测对嗜神经病毒进行分子筛查,狂犬病病毒、EHV-1、WEEV、VEEV、WNV 和黄病毒呈阴性,而检测到 MADV,Ct 值为 27.9 和 31.4。部分 NS1 和 E1 基因片段被扩增并测序。基于这两个基因的系统发育分析一致地将名为 Santo Antonio 的毒株置于 MADV 基因型 III 进化枝内,并在 E1 分析中得到了强有力的支持。这些病例发生在圣安东尼奥杜莱韦尔热附近的城郊地区,距离库亚巴约 30 公里,凸显了森林环境与人类改造环境之间的潜在界面。这些发现提供了巴西中西部 MADV 循环及其与马科疾病关联的分子证据。我们的研究结果强化了马作为嗜神经性虫媒病毒监测哨兵在到达人类之前的作用。

She joined the brand in 2021. People Editorial Guidelines Published on July 15, 2026 04:41PM EDT 1 Comment Laura Horton and the bat she found. Credit : Laura Horton/SWNS NEED TO KNOW Laura Horton used Google Lens to identify a bat she rescued and discovered potential rabies exposureThe AI tool prompted her to seek medical attention after noticing bite marks she hadn’t feltHorton hopes sharing her story raises awareness about rabies risks from wild animal encounters A woman is praising an AI tool for helping her seek life-saving treatment. In May 2026, Laura Horton — a 53-year-old personal trainer from Liverpool, England — was celebrating her birthday with a two-week vacation to Lesbos, Greece. On the fourth day of the trip, she noticed a bat was drowning in the swimming pool at the apartment complex she was staying in. Not thinking much of it, she decided to rescue the animal. “I grabbed it from the water on instinct because it was drowning — I had no idea of the risks,” she told Southwest News Service. “It sat on my hand for about 10 minutes, drying off.” “We all thought it looked cute, so I took a photo of it,” she added. The villa where Laura was bitten. Laura Horton/SWNS Our new app is here! Free, fun and full of exclusives. Scan to download now! After the bat flew away, Horton said she uploaded the photo to Google Lens — an AI tool that allows users to search what they see using their device’s camera — to figure out what species of bat it was. However, the results that came up were far from expected. “It started asking questions like, ‘Are those your hands?’ and ‘Have you washed your hands for 15 minutes after handling it?’” she recalled. “It warned me of the risk of rabies and said I wouldn’t feel a bite, as their teeth are too small.” “I thought it was all a bit dramatic,” she admitted. “But when I took a photo of my hand, I saw two tiny bite marks. I had no idea you could catch rabies from a bat.” Laura Horton holding the bat. Laura Horton/SWNS Related Stories Rabies Is Making a Comeback. Should You Be Worried? Organ Donor Unknowingly Gave Rabies to Cornea Graft Recipient as Well as Kidney Recipient Who Died Horton decided to call her healthcare provider the following day, which confirmed that she should seek medical attention. She was informed that she would need to receive the rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to prevent the virus from reaching her nervous system. She immediately went to a local hospital, but claimed that due to the language barrier, getting proper treatment was difficult. “At first, they tried to send me away with antibiotics. I’m not sure they understood what happened,” she said. “I was sent to a travel clinic, and a nurse was furious I hadn’t been given the first dose yet. I went back to the hospital and found the infectious diseases department – they were brilliant.” Bite marks on Laura Horton’s hand. Laura Horton/SWNS Sign up for From the Editor, our free weekly newsletter from PEOPLE’s Editor-in-Chief, Charlotte Triggs. While in Greece, Horton received two more shots before returning home on June 1 and receiving a fourth dose with her own doctor. “It was lucky Google Lens told me to go to hospital – who knows what might have happened,” she told the outlet. Laura Horton on vacation. Laura Horton/SWNS Never miss a story — sign up for PEOPLE’s free daily newsletter to stay up-to-date on the best of what PEOPLE has to offer​​, from celebrity news to compelling human interest stories. Horton said she’s been researching more about cases of rabies and is hoping that sharing her story will help others stay safe. “I read the tragic case about the boy in Canada who died after a bat landed on his face,” she said. “A lot of people aren’t aware of the dangers of these wild animals and the risks. Hopefully I can help raise awareness.” Laura Horton on vacation. Laura Horton/SWNS According to the Mayo Clinic, there’s no immediate sign that you’ve been infected with rabies, the deadly virus that’s nearly always spread to humans from contact with an infected animal. This is why doctors advise people to seek medical treatment immediately after any contact with a wild animal, and to undergo a series of rabies vaccines. Once symptoms begin to show, the condition is usually fatal. The incubation period depends on how far away from the brain the bite or scratch is, and how severe it is — and/or how much of the virus is transferred, the CDC warns. news.content: News Actions Facebook Tweet Email Montana Officials Warn Pet Owners To Stay Alert As Rabies Cases Rise This Summer Prev Next By: Logan Cyr Posted 10:58 PM, Jul 14, 2026 HELENA — Montana livestock officials are warning residents to stay alert for possible rabies exposure this summer as reports involving bats and other wildlife continue across the state. The Montana Department of Livestock says bats are the most common source of rabies cases in Montana, while skunks are typically linked to cases in southeastern parts of the state. 1/1 Skip Ad Continue watching after the ad Visit Advertiser website GO TO PAGE “So in Montana the 2 types of wildlife that we see with rabies are skunks in the southeastern part of the state and then bats statewide,” said Dr. Emily Kaleczyc, assistant state veterinarian with the Department of Livestock. State officials say there have been three confirmed rabid bats in Montana so far this year, including cases in Yellowstone, Gallatin and Flathead counties. The department also says it receives several calls a day involving pets or people exposed to wildlife. “A lot of human exposures, especially in Montana, are related to people finding bats in homes or cabins,” Kaleczyc said. Officials say anyone who may have been bitten or exposed to a bat should contact a doctor or public health official right away. They also warn that rabies does not always cause aggressive behavior in animals. Pets or livestock infected with rabies may simply act differently than normal. “Any changes in behavior, especially anything neurologic related, can be a sign of rabies in domestic species,” Kaleczyc said. State veterinarians say keeping pets and livestock vaccinated is the best way to prevent the disease. “So we have very effective vaccines against rabies for all of our domestic species, dogs, cats, all of our livestock species,” Kaleczyc said. Officials encourage anyone with questions or concerns about possible rabies exposure to contact the Montana Department of Livestock at 406-444-2976 or visit the department’s website. Founded in 1924 as the Office International des Epizooties (OIE), in May 2003 we adopted the common name World Organisation for Animal Health. An intergovernmental organisation, we focus on transparently disseminating information on animal diseases, improving animal health globally and thus build a safer, healthier and more sustainable world Mission Advocacy Strategy Structure and GovernanceToggle submenu Back to menu World Assembly Council Director General Governance Review Committee Organisation’s Framework Members Collaborate with us What we doToggle submenu Back to menuWhat we doWe work to improve animal health and welfare across the globe. Closed Captioning Information Manage Emails Apps Careers Search Q2News/ ktvq UCN2IWwjVxh4vOnMbnjiM8Hw News Montana Politics Montana Ag Network America 250 Your Health Matters More + Indian Country Positively Montana My MTN Contests Quick Links + News Montana Politics Montana Ag Network America 250 Your Health Matters Indian Country Positively Montana My MTN Contests News Actions Facebook Tweet Email Yellowstone County reports confirmed rabies case, officials stress pet vaccinations Prev Next Photo by: Facebook Post from Billings Animal Family Hospital By: Isabel Spartz Posted 3:04 AM, Jul 13, 2026 and last updated 4:02 PM, Jul 13, 2026 BILLINGS — State officials have confirmed a case of rabies in Yellowstone County, prompting veterinarians to remind residents to avoid contact with wildlife and ensure pets are current on their rabies vaccinations.The Montana Department of Livestock confirmed the case earlier this month. It is the first confirmed case in Yellowstone County this year and the third reported statewide in 2026.Watch the story here: Yellowstone County reports confirmed rabies case, officials stress pet vaccinations 1/1 Skip Ad Continue watchingafter the adVisit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGE Dr. Edie Best, owner and lead veterinarian at Billings Animal Family Hospital, said while rabies cases remain uncommon, the disease is nearly always fatal once symptoms develop, making prevention critical."Rabies is 100% fatal," Best said. "The one vaccination that is absolutely mandatory is the rabies vaccination."Rabies is a viral disease that affects the nervous system and can spread to both animals and humans through bites or scratches from infected animals. Health officials say residents should never approach or handle wild animals, particularly species known to carry the virus, including bats, skunks, raccoons, and foxes.Best said unusual behavior is often the first warning sign."If you see one of those animals out in the daytime or acting unusually, like a bat that's laying on the ground or a skunk that's out in the middle of the day, ... stay away," she said. "That's not normal."While human rabies infections are rare, any potential exposure should be treated as a medical emergency."If you get bit by that animal, that's an emergency room trip immediately," Best said. "The hard part about testing for rabies is the only way to test is to test the brain, so the animal has to be deceased."According to the Montana Department of Livestock, there have been 27 confirmed rabies detections in Montana since July 2025, all involving bats. The Yellowstone County case marks the county's first confirmed detection this year.Best said residents shouldn't panic but should remain aware of their surroundings, especially when spending time outdoors."We've always known it's out there," she said. "It's just a heads up. If you see something that really seems unusual, especially in one of those animals, it's probably not normal."
